title: Model
summary: A container that groups parts and other instances into one named object — characters, buildings, vehicles. Has its own CFrame via PivotTo/GetPivot, and PrimaryPart as its reference point.

properties.name: PrimaryPart
properties.description: The model's reference part (must be a direct child). Used by legacy MoveTo and as pivot fallback.

methods.name: GetPivot
methods.description: Current pivot CFrame (primary part, or bounding box center).

methods.name: PivotTo
methods.description: Moves the ENTIRE model so its pivot lands at the given CFrame — the modern way to move models.

methods.name: MoveTo
methods.description: Legacy: moves PrimaryPart to a position. Prefer PivotTo.

methods.name: BreakJoints / MakeJoints
methods.description: Disconnect/connect joints between the model's parts and the outside world.

details.heading: Models are not parts
details.body: A Model has no Size/Color/Transparency of its own — those belong to BaseParts. You can't tween a Model's position directly; move it with PivotTo or tween a PrimaryPart.

explanation.whatItIs: A labeled box around related objects. Group the 40 parts of a car into Model 'Car' and you can move, clone, and reference it as one thing.
explanation.whyItExists: Worlds are built from thousands of parts; grouping them keeps the hierarchy sane and lets systems act on whole assemblies.
whenToUse: Grouping any multi-part structure (buildings, vehicles, NPCs)
Player characters ARE models (with a Humanoid inside)
Spawn markers and zones as empty models with attributes
whenNotToUse: As a generic folder for organization — Folder is purpose-built and lighter
Expecting physics properties on the Model itself — those live on its parts
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Model "Car"
 ├─ Body (Part)            ← physics lives HERE
 ├─ Wheels (Parts)
 └─ PrimaryPart: Body

model:PivotTo(CFrame.new(0,10,0))
   → EVERY child moves together
```
tips: Set a PrimaryPart (or pivot) before moving with PivotTo for predictable placement
Detect 'is this a character?' with model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
PivotTo respects welds/joints — the whole assembly moves as one
commonMistakes: Treating a Model like a Part (model.Transparency? model.Position? — neither exists)
Forgetting to weld parts together before moving — unjoined parts get left behind
Using deprecated MoveTo when PivotTo gives precise orientation control

examples.title: Moving a model correctly
examples.code:
local car = workspace.Car

-- Move the whole car 20 studs up, keeping orientation:
car:PivotTo(car:GetPivot() + Vector3.new(0, 20, 0))

-- Teleport to a spawn pad with orientation:
local pad = workspace.CarSpawn
car:PivotTo(pad.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0))

examples.title: Character detection via model + humanoid
examples.code:
local function isCharacter(model)
    return model:IsA("Model") and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") ~= nil
end

for _, child in workspace:GetChildren() do
    if isCharacter(child) then
        print("Character found:", child.Name)
    end
end
